tells.1: Relentlessly polished rhetorical escalation, culminating in an elaborate metaphor about risk moving somewhere less visible.
tells.2: The neatly staged closing reversal—“It didn't. It moved”—feels manufactured.
tells.4: Repeated punchy fragments and redundant declarations make the conversational voice feel engineered.
tells.5: “I get less of the thinking” sounds like an unnatural paraphrase retained to preserve a rhetorical contrast.
tells.6: The closing trio “cheaper, more rushed, less visible” and billing punchline feel formulaic.

reason: Version 2 has the strongest balance of readable structure, concrete explanation, and personal voice; version 6 comes close but needs paragraph breaks. Version 3 feels the most spontaneous, but its repetition, grammatical slips, and categorical claims make it the least convincing as skilled, publication-ready writing; these stylistic judgments do not establish authorship.
